text:
IncidentBot: alert: elevated 5xxs and queue growth on runner-prod (action-exec path). probable correlation with high external-action fanout from customers in eu-west-1. auto-detect: function-exec error rate 18% over 5m. paging eng-runtime-oncall @Maya

Maya Nguyen: seeing 5xx and long tail latencies on /v1/actions/exec, memory pressure creeping on pods. customers spiking -> queuing.

TJ Patel: can we throttle action calls per-tenant as a quick mitigation? prioritize text-gen endpoints.

Maya Nguyen: agreed. plan: 1) soft-rate-limit action-exec globally to 50rps 2) per-tenant emergency caps for top offenders 3) disable structured-output (json-mode) for non-enterprise plans to reduce parsing cost 4) monitor errors and rollback if regress.

Dan H: ready to run change. who has permissions for live config? I can run redwoodctl but need guardrails.

Rachel S: I’ll draft comms for impacted customers (top 10) after we have tenant list. SupportBot, can you surface top traffic by tenant in last 10m?

SupportBot: pulled top tenants: acme-corp, betaapp, shoply, edu-svc. acme-corp = 42% of action-exec QPS from eu-west-1. Links: https://internal.metrics/runner-prod/top-tenants

Maya Nguyen: ok executing staged change. Dan, run these commands in sequence and paste outputs. first command:

```
# soft global cap on action-exec
redwoodctl runtime set-rate --scope global --route /v1/actions/exec --rps 50 --reason "emergency degrade"
```

TJ Patel: also add per-tenant cap for acme-corp to 8rps

```
redwoodctl runtime set-rate --scope tenant:acme-corp --route /v1/actions/exec --rps 8 --reason "hot-tenant mitigation"
```

Dan H: running global cap -> OK, rollout started to eu-west-1 (canary 10%).

IncidentBot: deploy note: rollout 10% -> 100% over 90s, target rps=50.

Dan H: global cap reached 100% now. observing initial drop in QPS and CPU trend down.

Leo C: enabling structured-output fallback: for non-enterprise plans, force text-only responses for action-exec to reduce serializer CPU. command:

```
redwoodctl runtime set-config --key action_exec.json_mode --value "disabled" --scope plan:free,plan:pro
```

Emily R: FYI this will break customers relying on JSON schema output. we need to mark those as impacted and put in support ticket template.

Maya Nguyen: acknowledged. Support, flag any enterprise customers if they need structured output exempted.

SupportBot: enterprise tenants exempt list: acme-corp is enterprise -> NOT exempt by default. Requesting manual override allowance.

Rachel S: hold on enterprise exemption for acme-corp — they are the top offender. propose to keep them capped but allow structured output for enterprise customers that opt in via support-approved bypass.

TJ Patel: adding circuit to allow enterprise bypass with rate-limited token. command to create bypass token:

```
redwoodctl runtime create-bypass --tenant acme-corp --route /v1/actions/exec --rps 20 --token EXEMPT-XXXXX
```

Dan H: bypass token created, but not dispatched. we should not enable until comms + risk review.

Maya Nguyen: monitoring: error rate down to 6%, tail latency p95 from 1.4s -> 700ms. queuing dropped 70%. good.

IncidentBot: note: customer-impact assessment in progress. initial: several low-tier customers saw malformed outputs due to json-mode toggle, ~12 support tickets predicted. No major data loss.

Rachel S: drafting message to impacted customers: short notice, mitigation actions taken, ETA for rollback, contact link, and opt-in enterprise path. Will post in ~10m.

Emily R: ops question — do we need to adjust Dedicated pools? some dedicated nodes still spiking in memory.

Leo C: scheduled auto-scale is delayed due to quota -> manually draining highest mem pods. command:

```
kubectl drain pod/runner-prod-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

Maya Nguyen: handing off to night oncall @TJ in 20m. TJ please keep the global cap and acme cap for now. If error rate <3% and stable for 15m, consider relaxing to 80rps global.

TJ Patel: taking handoff. will monitor for 30m, keep support loop. tagging @SupportBot to push ticket template.

SupportBot: posted ticket template to support channel and created drafts for top 10 tenants.

Maya Nguyen: final note — we kept feature disabled at plan level rather than code path toggle to reduce blast radius. document mitigation steps in incident runbook and add postmortem hook to evaluate root cause (mostly a runaway external-action pattern).

Dan H: saving logs and traces:
```
redwoodctl traces query --service runner-prod --since 15m > /tmp/runner-prod-traces.log
```

Maya Nguyen: thanks all. handoff complete. paging cleared. :white_check_mark:

TJ Patel: will keep an eye. if acme requests bypass, coordinate with product and support for a controlled rollout.

IncidentBot: incident state -> mitigated, monitoring.

Maya Nguyen: postmortem: required. assign to eng-runtime team. cc @Rachel S for comms follow-up.

Rachel S: acknowledged, I'll draft postmortem and customer notes.

SupportBot: tickets queued and assigned.

Dan H: moving logs to /artifacts/incidents/2620001234/

Maya Nguyen: good job team.
